name: My Roommate Is a Ghost
blurb: A cheap flat comes with a polite ghost, three rules and a cupboard she must never open
title: My Roommate Is a Ghost: Short Drama Script (Episode 1)
description: A free 2.5-minute vertical supernatural romcom short drama script for 3 actors. A cheap flat comes with a polite ghost who has rules. Free to film.
h1: My Roommate Is a Ghost: a 2.5-Minute Supernatural Romcom Script, Episode 1
logline: Tess finds a flat at a third of the normal rent and soon finds out why: Henry, a very polite ghost with strong opinions about tea, lives there too. He has three rules, a landlord wants to sell in thirty days, and both of them need the flat to survive.
setting: One old flat: kitchen, living room and hallway with a cupboard. Props: a kettle, mugs, a moving box, a coat, papers, an old black and white photo, a cup of tea.

roles.name: Tess
roles.note: Mid 20s, broke and stubborn, too poor to be scared for long.

roles.name: Henry
roles.note: 30s in appearance, a ghost from the sixties; polite, fussy, lonely, secretly romantic.

roles.name: Mr. Pell
roles.note: 60s, the landlord; cheerful about money, nervous about the flat. Any gender.

script.action: TESS, mid twenties, unpacks a box of mugs. The kettle clicks on by itself. She freezes. A second mug slides an inch across the counter.

script.say: Milk before the water? In my kitchen?

script.action: Tess screams and spins round. HENRY, thirties, in a faded old-fashioned suit, sits politely on the counter. He raises a hand.

script.say: Please don't run. The last four did, and the stairs are very steep.
You're a... you're see-through.
Slightly. Only in bright light. I'm Henry. I was here first.
The advert said quiet and cheap!
I am quiet. And you're paying a third of the normal rent. That's me. I'm the discount.

script.action: Tess grabs her coat, then stops. She looks at her bank app. Groans. Puts the coat down.

script.say: I can't afford to run. Fine. What do you want?
Three rules.
One. Knock before you come into the kitchen. Two. No sad songs after ten, I can't bear them. Three. Never open the hall cupboard.
What's in the hall cupboard?
That is rule three.

script.scene: INT. OLD FLAT – LIVING ROOM – NEXT DAY

script.action: MR. PELL, sixties, the landlord, waves papers at Tess. Behind him, Henry pulls faces. Tess bites back a laugh.

script.say: Good news. A developer wants the whole building. In thirty days it's sold, it's knocked down, and you get your deposit back.
Thirty days? I just moved in!
Nobody stays here more than two nights anyway. Strange noises.

script.action: Henry stops pulling faces. He stares at the floor. Pell leaves.

script.say: If they knock it down, what happens to you?
I don't know. I can't leave the flat. I've tried. I'm waiting for someone. She promised she'd come back.
How long ago?
Sixty-one years. She's late.
Then we stop the sale. I need this flat, you need more time. Partners?
I can't shake hands. But yes. Partners.

script.action: Tess passes the hall cupboard with a cup of tea. It creaks. Its door swings open on its own.

script.say: Tess, don't look...

script.action: Too late. On the shelf inside: an old black and white photo of a young woman in a sixties dress. She has Tess's face. Exactly.
Tess picks it up and turns it over. Faded ink on the back.

script.say: Henry. Why is my name on the back of this photo?

script.action: Henry appears in the doorway. He doesn't answer. He just looks at her as if she has finally come home.

body: Shoot vertical 9:16 in one flat over one evening and one afternoon. Keep the phone on a tripod for every shot with Henry; a still camera makes him feel like part of the room. Light Tess with a warm lamp and Henry with a cooler light such as a laptop screen just out of frame. For the floating mug, tie clear fishing line to it and pull from off camera, and do five or six takes. Print the old photo by turning a picture of the actress black and white and ageing it with tea. Record the voice-from-nowhere line with Henry off camera so it sounds disembodied.

ul: Henry is a perfect host stuck in the wrong century. Play him fussy and formal, never spooky; the comedy is his manners.
Tess's fear lasts exactly until she checks her bank balance. That turn from terror to resignation is the first big laugh.
Mr. Pell must never look at Henry. Rehearse the faces behind his back so Pell genuinely cannot see them coming.
Slow down on Sixty-one years. She's late. It is the moment the comedy turns tender; give it a breath on each side.
In the final scene Henry says nothing. All of the story is in his face; do not let him rush to speak or move.
Common mistake: playing the photo reveal as horror. Tess is shaken and curious, not screaming; it is a romance cliffhanger.
Set it in a student dorm room or a rented room above a shop, with the ghost as a former student or the shop's old owner.
Swap genders so the new tenant is a young man and the ghost a polite woman from the sixties, or add a flatmate who cannot see her.
Change the cliffhanger: the name on the back of the photo is not Tess but her grandmother, which means Henry was waiting for someone in her family.

prompts.keyframe: A young woman unpacking mugs in a small old kitchen at night freezes as a kettle switches on by itself, a faint translucent man in a vintage suit sitting on the counter behind her, warm lamp light, cinematic still, vertical 9:16.
shots: Close-up of a mug sliding slowly across a kitchen counter by itself, the camera tilts up to a young woman's frozen, wide-eyed face; warm lamp light, creepy but playful mood, vertical 9:16.

Medium shot: a polite translucent man in a vintage suit sits on a kitchen counter counting rules on his fingers while a young woman presses against the fridge; static frame, comic tension, vertical 9:16.
Wide living room shot by day: a landlord waves papers at a young woman while the ghost pulls faces behind him, she tries not to laugh; handheld, light comedy, vertical 9:16.
Dim hallway at night: a cupboard door creaks open on its own, the young woman lifts an old black and white photo and turns it over; slow push in, eerie romantic suspense, vertical 9:16.

faq.q: How do I make Henry look like a ghost without effects?
faq.a: You do not need effects. Dress him in old clothes, keep him very still, light him a little cooler than Tess and never let Mr. Pell look at him. The kettle and the mug can be moved off camera with fishing line or a hidden hand.

faq.q: Can I use it on a monetised channel?
faq.a: Yes. The script is free under CC BY 4.0, including commercial use. Credit "Script: cv.cm" in the caption or the closing card.

faq.q: Is it too scary for a school project?
faq.a: No. It is a romcom with one spooky moment and nothing graphic. The ghost is polite and the creepiest thing in it is an old photo, so it works for class or a school film club.
